seoTitle: Free Git Command Builder and Cheat Sheet Online
metaDescription: Pick a Git task and fill in a few parameters to get the exact command, an explanation and a warning for destructive operations. Free, in your browser.
intro: Offers a list of common Git tasks such as undo, squash, rebase, cherry-pick, safe force push, bisect and sparse clone, and builds the exact command with a short explanation and a warning for risky operations.
why: Git has a command for everything and a memory for nothing: is it reset --soft or --mixed, how do you force-push without destroying a colleague's work, what was the flag for a sparse clone? Searching the answer again each time breaks your flow. This tool works as a cheat sheet that fills in the blanks. Choose the task, type up to three parameters such as a branch name, commit hash or number of commits, and get the command with a one-line explanation. Operations that rewrite history or throw work away carry a warning. It does not run anything or touch your repository, so you copy the command into your own terminal when you are ready. It all runs in your browser.
howTo: Choose the task from the list, for example "Squash last N commits into one".
Fill in the parameters the task asks for, such as the number of commits or a branch name.
Read the command and its explanation, then copy it into your terminal.

faq.q: Does the tool run Git commands?
faq.a: No. It only generates text. Nothing touches your repository, and you decide when and where to run the command.

Undoing and amending commits, branches, stash, interactive rebase, squash, cherry-pick, revert, safe force push, shallow and sparse clones, bisect, history searches, reflog recovery, clean, restore and tags.
git push --force-with-lease refuses to overwrite remote commits you have not seen, which is safer than a plain force push when a colleague may have pushed.

faq.q: What if I leave a parameter empty?
faq.a: The command contains a readable placeholder, such as a commit hash in angle brackets or path/to/file, so it is obvious what is missing. Replace the placeholder before you run the command.
